projects.name: Autonomous Swarm Robotics for Nuclear Decommissioning - Google DeepMind
projects.description:
Completed an eight-week research internship through the Google DeepMind Research Ready Programme in collaboration with the University of York, developing an autonomous swarm robotics system for nuclear decommissioning. Built a ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo simulation environment for TurtleBot3 robots, working alongside the team on the Cache Consensus decentralised coordination algorithm for autonomous waste clustering. I contributed to the integration and validation of the autonomy stack across simulation and physical hardware, evaluating the sim-to-real gap and system behaviour under real-world deployment.

I led the design and data collection for a computer vision pipeline targeting nuclear waste classification and localisation, overseeing the fine-tuning of a YOLOv8 object detector and implementing ground-plane homography to convert image detections into spatial coordinates. The project also investigated the safety assurance of autonomous ML-enabled robotic systems, combining RoboStar principles for robotics software and control with AMLAS for ML assurance. I applied these methodologies to support the verification, robustness and safety assurance of the overall system.

projects.name: UKSEDS Olympus Rover Trials Advanced Stream
projects.description:
Competed in the UKSEDS Olympus Rover Trials – Advanced Stream, developing a rover capable of autonomously navigating a planetary-style environment and collecting regolith samples. Over nine months, I led the autonomy subteam, overseeing the development and integration of the rover's software and perception systems.

We developed a ROS 2-based autonomous navigation stack integrating LiDAR and RGB-D camera data for perception, with Nav2 used for autonomous navigation and motion planning. The team also developed a Gazebo simulation environment to enable early testing and iterative development before deployment to physical hardware. A key engineering challenge was optimising the autonomy stack for resource-constrained deployment on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and custom PCB, where the system successfully operated during the competition.

As Autonomy Subteam Lead, I coordinated software development with the mechanical and electrical teams, delegated technical work and drove architectural decisions through iterative performance evaluation. This involved balancing algorithmic performance, hardware limitations and system-level integration requirements to deliver a functioning autonomous rover within the competition timeline.

projects.name: Wearable Knee Exoskeleton for Sit-to-Stand Assistance
projects.description: Collaborated in a team of 5 over eight months to design, prototype and evaluate a wearable knee exoskeleton for assisting sit-to-stand (STS) transitions. The project began with an extensive literature review covering biomechanics, soft exoskeletons, Twisted String Actuators (TSAs), reinforcement learning, and human-robot interaction before progressing through system design, hardware prototyping, simulation and experimental validation. My primary contribution focused on the simulation and control framework. I assisted in developing a MyoSuite/MuJoCo-based musculoskeletal simulation of the STS movement using a four-phase reflex controller (momentum lean, seat-off, extension and stabilisation), enabling realistic lower-body motion. I also modelled a physics-based Twisted String Actuator (TSA) with nonlinear contraction geometry, motor speed-torque dynamics, cable slack detection and RK4 numerical integration before integrating it into the simulation as an assistive knee torque source. To optimise assistance, I implemented Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) using Stable-Baselines3, jointly learning TSA string length and staggered motor activation timings through a reward function balancing quadriceps muscle reduction, trajectory tracking, movement stability and completion time. The optimised policy achieved a 10% reduction in quadriceps muscle activation compared to the unassisted baseline. I also developed the real-time intention detection pipeline running on a Raspberry Pi, where IMU data from an ICM-20948 sensor was fused using a Madgwick filter and processed by a rule-based finite state machine (FSM) that robustly detected STS initiation with 84.38% accuracy from trunk kinematics using orientation, angular velocity, acceleration, temporal gating and cooldown constraints to minimise false activations.

projects.name: Multi-Modal SLAM: Visual Odometry & LiDAR Mapping (COMP0222)
projects.description: Developed a multi-modal Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) system as part of the UCL COMP0222 coursework, combining visual and LiDAR-based approaches to reconstruct environments and estimate trajectories in real time. For visual SLAM, a continuous stream of RGB frames was captured using an Intel RealSense D455 depth camera and processed through both COLMAP (Structure-from-Motion) and ORB-SLAM2 pipelines; frames were extracted at 5 fps and 10 fps respectively, with trajectories exported in TUM format and quantitatively evaluated using evo (APE and RPE metrics). COLMAP leveraged a FAISS-indexed vocabulary tree for scalable image retrieval and feature matching across keyframes. For 2D LiDAR SLAM, scan data was collected on an RPLIDAR A2M12 and aligned incrementally using a point-to-plane ICP scan-to-local-map formulation, with loop closure detected via a two-stage pipeline: spatial proximity filtering followed by a rotation-invariant range histogram descriptor compared using chi-squared distance, verified by ICP inlier ratio before committing a pose-graph edge. An occupancy grid map was built in parallel from the same LiDAR scans to produce a probabilistic 2D floor plan of the environment.

projects.name: InfluX - Social Trends Analytics Platform
projects.description: Developed InfluX, a social trend intelligence platform that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to surface real-time insights from social and search data. The system ingests data via AWS Strands and the Google Search API, with a FastAPI backend orchestrating retrieval, processing and analysis. Retrieved content is embedded using FAISS and clustered with HDBSCAN to identify emerging themes, which are then visualised as interactive graphs and summarised into clear, human-readable insights using an LLM. Built during the AgentVerse Hackathon 2025, the project was awarded 2nd place for its novel approach to trend discovery and analysis.

projects.name: Àgbẹ̀ - Autonomous Agricultural Robot for Precision Seeding
projects.description: During a 6-week internship with the National Center for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in Abuja, Nigeria, I prototyped a modular agricultural robot equipped with Wi-Fi monitoring. The system integrates seed-dispensing and furrow-opening mechanisms, and leverages GPS-IMU-Encoder sensor fusion through a Kalman filter for precise navigation. To enhance usability and scalability, I designed a modular interface for different field tasks and implemented ESP8266-based wireless telemetry for real-time monitoring and diagnostics, resulting in improved planting accuracy and throughput compared to traditional methods.

projects.name: Protalab - Agentic AI Workflow for Automated 3D Printing
projects.description: Participated in a project with four of my peers in collaboration with Outshift by Cisco, to highlight agentic capabilities for real life solutions. We designed and implemented an agentic workflow using LangChain and LangGraph, enabling modular coordination of LLM-based agents for design generation, refinement, 3D printing and supervision.

projects.name: UKSEDS Olympus Rover Trials Basic Stream
projects.description: Designed and manufactured a tracked robot rover equipped with a teleoperated, camera-mounted arm for navigating simulated Martian terrain. The rover was controlled via Wi-Fi from a custom mobile interface and featured autonomous QR code recognition and decoding, implemented using MicroPython and Computer Vision on the Nicla Vision Module. This innovative combination of teleoperation and automation earned us 2nd place in the competition and the 'Best Automation' award for our automatic image capture and processing system.

projects.name: Cartpole Control System (COMP0216)
projects.description: Designed, simulated, and physically implemented an inverted pendulum cartpole system as part of a team of four. Applied model-based systems engineering to guide development and implemented three advanced control strategies - PID, LQR with pole placement, and sliding mode control - benchmarked across custom Python and Gazebo simulations. The final prototype integrated a Kalman filter for state estimation and demonstrated real-time balancing using an embedded Arduino-based controller.

projects.name: Robotic Gripper Simulation and Grasp Success Prediction with Machine Learning (COMP0213)
projects.description: Created a robotic gripper simulation tool using Python and PyBullet, capable of generating grasp data and evaluating grasp success for multiple gripper types and objects. Key features include realistic physics simulation, customizable parameters, automated success/failure evaluation, and random approach angle generation. Implemented success prediction using machine learning techniques, such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines and Multilayer Perceptron

projects.name: Spotlight - First Place Project at Google Black Googler Network Hackathon
projects.description: Participated in Google's BGN Hackathon and developed a web application that highlights Black innovators in engineering, securing both 1st place and 'People's Choice' awards. The application incorporated Google Cloud Vision AI for real-time object detection and the Gemini API for contextual information, utilizing Cloud Storage Triggers for automated image processing.

projects.name: Machine Learning for Classification and Regression (COMP0214)
projects.description: Analyzing Navigation Data for Alzheimer's Disease Detection: An investigation into the use of navigation patterns to differentiate individuals with Alzheimer's Disease (AD) from a control group. Binary Classification with sklearn was utilised to classify AD patients. WIFI Signal for Indoor Localisation: This component of the coursework focused on predicting indoor X-Y coordinates using Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) values from Wi-Fi access points. A neural network was designed and trained using Pytorch to predict the X-Y coordinates accurately.

projects.name: Sign Language Fingerspelling Recognition with Computer Vision
projects.description: This project is an application designed to recognise and translate ASL (American Sign Language) fingerspelling into corresponding text. It leverages machine learning and computer vision techniques, drawing inspiration from personal experiences with sign language and DeepMind's Project Euphonia, which uses AI to restore speech for individuals with communication difficulties like those with ALS. The application utilises an MLP (Multilayer Perceptron) model built with TensorFlow, which processes hand landmarks obtained from Google's MediaPipe open-source framework. This trained model then classifies and translates ASL fingerspelling gestures in real-time.
